blanks.sentence: Wildfires are uncontrolled fires in places such as _____.
They are common in _____ such as Spain.
Today’s fires are worse partly because rising temperatures are caused by _____.
Forests have grown _____ because too few animals feed on the vegetation.
Dense _____ makes forests more likely to catch fire.
European ecosystems used to include _____ such as bison and wild horses.
Some of those animals disappeared from ecosystems because of _____ and domestication.
Rewilding Spain has brought back herds of _____ to central Spanish forests.
The cows help because of their _____ and their trampling.
Each tauros can eat over _____ of plant material per day.

multipleChoice.question: How are wildfires defined in the programme?
options: Small planned fires used to manage farms
Unplanned fires in places such as forests or grasslands that spread uncontrollably
Fires that happen only inside cities
Natural fires that never involve human activity

multipleChoice.question: What has made today’s wildfires especially severe?
options: Lower rainfall caused by cows
The disappearance of television animal heroes
Too many people planting seagrass
Rising temperatures linked to climate change

multipleChoice.question: Why have some forests become more fire-prone?
options: There are not enough animals eating the trees, bushes and grass
People have removed all vegetation from forests
The forests have become too wet to manage
The trees have stopped growing completely

multipleChoice.question: Which animals are given as examples of former big grazers in Europe?
options: Dolphins, kangaroos and dogs
Sharks, turtles and wildebeest
Bison, tauros and wild horses
Cows, goats and sheep only

multipleChoice.question: What is the result of fewer grazing wild animals?
options: Grasslands stop growing and fires disappear
Forests and grasslands keep growing unchecked, increasing wildfire risk
Domestic cows become extinct immediately
Spain becomes cooler and wetter

multipleChoice.question: What has Pablo reintroduced into central Spanish forests?
options: Modern fire engines driven by farmers
Herds of wild horses from Australia
Sea turtles that protect seagrass
Herds of tauros similar to extinct aurochs

multipleChoice.question: How does trampling help reduce fire risk?
options: It opens up the forest so flammable vegetation is less densely packed
It turns all vegetation into water
It makes the cows eat less each day
It prevents every future wildfire in Spain

multipleChoice.question: What does Beth say tauros eat?
options: Only grass and nothing else
Only food provided by humans
Grass, leaves, tree branches and bark
Mostly insects and small animals

multipleChoice.question: What does the figure “over 30 kilos a day” suggest about tauros?
options: They are too small to affect the forest
Their eating can remove a large amount of vegetation
They eat only when fires begin
They need helmets to work safely

multipleChoice.question: What is the programme’s overall point about cows in Spain?
options: They fight fires in the same way as human firefighters
They make wildfires more destructive by eating trees
Their grazing and movement can help manage vegetation that fuels fires
They replace the need for all climate action
